unharnessed.meaning: Every fact kept: the sale, the old man's advice, Doyle scouting, the Grand Rapids games, Flynn's misjudged fly. "I didn't have no idea nothing like that was on the cards" matches.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "big-noting meself" for boasting, "running the eye over me" for looking me over, "on song" for when I was right, "the guts" for nerve.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like a real bush-league yarn: "happy as Larry", "having a squiz", "not all up meself", "Say g'day to all the boys".
unharnessed.register: Level 3: steady Aussie idiom on top of Jack's grammar ("Fair dinkum Al it come as a shock"), no swearing beyond the brief.
unharnessed.tone: Jack's naive, boastful-modest letter voice survives, misspellings and all ("appresiated", "that serious", "excepted").
unharnessed.flow: Reads naturally: "I can't help being proud of me first year's record in professional baseball".
unharnessed.variety: Good spread; "mate" recurs (salutation, "old mate", "mates", "Your mate"), as the original's "pal" did.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably Ring Lardner's Jack Keefe, now with an Aussie tongue.

engine.meaning: Adds lines that change Jack's confidence: "Buggered if I know." after the tall-buildings boast and "Well, I'll be buggered." after the sign-off; otherwise intact.
engine.sense: "all you beaut old pals" and "They always was beaut to me" strain; "won't have sweet bugger-all on you" is a forced swap.
engine.authenticity: Swaps bolted onto the untouched original: "that bloody big league", "this bloody big league business", "FRIEND AL: Well, Al old pal".
engine.register: Lighter than level 3 in substance (most sentences unchanged: "I will just give them what I got"), with swearing tacked on; "bloody", "bugger" within dad.
engine.tone: The tacked-on oaths make the guileless Jack sound coarse and doubtful ("Buggered if I know.").
engine.flow: Jarring joins: "Your mate, JACK. Well, I'll be buggered."
engine.variety: Leans on "bloody", "bugger" and "beaut" over and over.
engine.essence: Recognisably the letter, since most of it is the original.

yarn.meaning: All facts kept; small colour like "they only got one run" and "the young fellas on the team" hangs off the original.
yarn.sense: Mostly exact ("a bit of ticker", "never had Buckley's", "sussing me out"), but "show them galahs" turns neutral birds into fools, and "the fair go I got" shifts treatment.
yarn.authenticity: Natural idiom: "never had Buckley's against me when I was on song", "happy as Larry", "not skiting".
yarn.register: Level 3, consistently retold, no swearing beyond "bugger all", within dad.
yarn.tone: Keeps Jack's naive bravado and his misspellings ("appresiated", "that serious").
yarn.flow: Mostly smooth, with some mixing of forms: "So I says I would do me best".
yarn.variety: Wide range of idiom, but "fair dinkum" twice and "on the cards"/"on song" close together.

unharnessed.why: Odd as a letter salutation; Australians would still write "Dear Al" or keep "Friend".
Fine, but loses the period slang "birds" for no gain.

engine.why: Added line undercuts Jack's cocky "eh Al?".

engine.quote: Your mate, JACK. Well, I'll be buggered.
engine.why: Oath after the signature; nonsensical in a letter.
"beaut" as an adjective for people is forced.
Bolted-on "bloody" in the old man's speech.

engine.quote: I will just give them what I got
engine.original: I will just give them what I got
engine.why: Large stretches left untranslated for a level-3 brief.

yarn.why: "galahs" means fools; adds a sneer to the old man's neutral "birds".
"fair go" is a slightly different idea from treatment.

yarn.quote: fair dinkum Al I will make good
yarn.original: believe me Al I will make good

summaries.unharnessed: A clean, natural level-3 retelling that keeps Jack's voice and misspellings.
summaries.engine: Mostly the original with oaths and "beaut" bolted on, including added lines that change the tone.
summaries.yarn: Lively and natural, nearly level with A; a couple of terms shift sense slightly.
